facts.statement: The first specimens of Gobipteryx were discovered in 1971 during a Polish-Mongolian expedition to the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: The first specimens were two damaged skulls discovered as part of the 1971 Polish-Mongolian Paleontological Expedition to the Gobi Desert by Dr. Teresa Maryańska

facts.statement: Gobipteryx was reclassified as an enantiornithes bird in 1981 after Dr. Cyril Walker defined that clade.
facts.quote: However, in 1981, Dr. Cyril Walker defined the clade enantiornithes and Gobipteryx was reclassified as an enantiornithes bird

facts.statement: A species named Nanantius valifanovi was later identified as a misidentified specimen of Gobipteryx minuta.
facts.quote: In 1996, Evgeny Kurochkin described a new bird known as Nanantius valifanovi also from the Barun Goyot Formation. However, it was later discovered that N. valifanoi was actually a new misidentified specimen of Gobipteryx minuta

facts.statement: Gobipteryx lived during the Campanian Age of the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Gobipteryx (from "Gobi" [referring to the Gobi Desert where it was first discovered], and Greek pteryx "wing") is a genus of prehistoric bird from the Campanian Age of the Late Cretaceous Period

facts.statement: Gobipteryx fossils date from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: With a skull length of 45 millimeters, Gobipteryx was approximately the size of a partridge.
facts.quote: Based on a skull length of 45 millimeters, Gobipteryx has been estimated to be approximately the size of a partridge

facts.statement: Gobipteryx possessed a toothless beak formed by fused premaxillae bones.
facts.quote: Gobipteryx has a toothless beak formed from the fusion of the premaxillae bones

facts.statement: Gobipteryx is thought to have had superprecocial development, allowing it to fly immediately upon hatching.
facts.quote: Gobipteryx, along with other enantiornithes, is thought to have superprecocial development, in which it was capable of flying upon hatching

facts.statement: The near-complete ossification of forelimbs and shoulders in advanced embryos supports the theory that Gobipteryx could fly at hatching.
facts.quote: Evidence for this comes from the fact that the forelimbs and shoulders of advanced embryos are almost completely ossified

facts.statement: Gobipteryx fossils were first found in the Lower Nemegt Beds of the Barun Goyot Formation in the Nemegt Basin.
facts.quote: It was first found in the sandstones of the Lower Nemegt Beds of the Barun Goyot Formation of the Nemegt Basin

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Gobipteryx consisted of at least 19 presacral vertebrae, with the last six being dorsals.
facts.quote: The vertebral column consists of at least 19 presacral vertebrae, the last six of these being dorsals

facts.statement: Gobipteryx's ulna was approximately twice as thick as its radius.
facts.quote: Gobipteryx's ulna is about twice as thick as the radius

facts.statement: Seven advanced embryos of Gobipteryx minuta were found during the 1971 expedition, including two skeletons in the Khermeen Tsav redbeds.
facts.quote: Also during the 1971 Polish-Mongolian Paleontological Expedition to the Gobi Desert, in which the first specimens were found, advanced embryos of Gobipteryx minuta were found. Seven specimens in total were found, including two skeletons in the redbeds of Khermeen Tsav in Mongolia's Gobi Desert

facts.statement: Growth in G. minuta slowed immediately after hatching, suggesting high mobility focused energy on locomotion.
facts.quote: In addition, the growth of G. minuta has been shown to slow down immediately following hatching

rejected.statement: Dr. Andrzej Elżanowski first described Gobipteryx in 1974 based on a single damaged skull now housed in Warsaw.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen is housed at the Institute of Paleobiology of the Polish Academy of Sciences in Warsaw, Poland and was first described by Dr. Andrzej Elżanowski using a single damaged skull

rejected.statement: Gobipteryx is believed to have been capable of flight due to its long scapula providing extensive muscle attachment area.
rejected.quote: Gobipteryx is believed to have been capable of flight. The scapula is long, and therefore, well suited for flight by having more area for muscle attachment
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is believed to have been capable of flight'

rejected.statement: The neural spines of the twelfth and thirteenth vertebrae formed a nuchal blade, the highest point of the vertebral column.
rejected.quote: The neural spines of the twelfth and thirteenth vertebrae form the nuchal blade, which represents the point of greatest elevation in the vertebral column
